headline: Massachusetts lawmakers seek FAA review before Amazon drones launch in Westborough
dek: The congressional delegation wants a site-specific environmental assessment and public comment before Prime Air begins package deliveries from the MetroWest town.
body: Four members of Massachusetts’ congressional delegation are asking Amazon and the Federal Aviation Administration to complete a site-specific environmental review before the company begins drone deliveries from its Westborough fulfillment center. Sens. Ed Markey and Elizabeth Warren and Reps. Jim McGovern and Lori Trahan sent letters Wednesday seeking an assessment of noise, safety, privacy and other local effects, according to [Markey’s announcement](https://www.markey.senate.gov/news/press-releases/-sens-markey-warren-reps-mcgovern-trahan-demand-faa-amazon-study-impacts-of-amazons-westborough-mass-drone-program-before-launching-drone-delivery).

The request is aimed at a proposed Prime Air launch facility at Amazon’s existing site at 64 Otis Street. The lawmakers want residents to have a public-comment opportunity before the FAA authorizes operations. Their letters ask Amazon and the FAA to respond by Oct. 29; they also ask for an explanation and any Westborough-specific analysis if the agencies decline a local review. The letters describe the request as a response to community concerns, not as a ruling that the project has been approved or that deliveries are imminent.

The proposed operation would be large enough to affect more than the immediate warehouse property. [Boston.com reported](https://www.boston.com/news/local-news/2026/10/14/before-amazon-drones-take-off-in-westborough-lawmakers-want-more-answers/) that Amazon hopes eventually to make as many as 1,000 deliveries a day from the facility. The drones could carry packages weighing up to five pounds within a 7.5-mile radius, reaching parts of Worcester and nearby communities. [WBUR](https://www.wbur.org/news/2026/10/14/amazon-drone-delivery-massachusetts-markey-trahan-mcgovern) reported that the planned aircraft weigh about 80 pounds, can travel as fast as 74 mph and could serve parts of Shrewsbury, Northborough, Grafton, Worcester, Sutton and Southborough.

That reach is why the dispute is not simply a question about an accessory structure in a warehouse parking lot. Residents and officials have raised questions about the frequency of flights, routes, operating hours, noise, privacy, safety, cybersecurity and environmental effects. The [Town of Westborough’s project page](https://www.westboroughma.gov/1541/Prime-Air-Drone-Delivery-Service-Applica) says the proposal has drawn regional interest from communities including Ashland, Berlin, Boylston, Grafton, Hopkinton, Hudson, Marlborough, Millbury, Northborough, Shrewsbury, Southborough, Sutton, Upton, West Boylston and Worcester.

The lawmakers’ federal argument centers on the FAA’s nationwide environmental review for expanded commercial drone package delivery. They say that framework does not adequately address Westborough’s historic town center, local environmental conditions, Massachusetts weather and daylight, or the risks associated with transporting hazardous materials. WBUR reported that the FAA’s earlier environmental assessments covered 23 states but none in New England. Massachusetts has joined 14 other states and Harris County, Texas, in a lawsuit challenging the nationwide finding, according to Westborough’s project page and the lawmakers’ statement.

Federal review is only one track. Westborough retains authority over local land-use questions, while the FAA controls the national airspace and federal aviation approvals. The town says its building commissioner classified the proposed Prime Air operation as an accessory use to the existing fulfillment center, leaving site-plan review with the Planning Board at this stage. Several residents appealed that interpretation; if the Zoning Board of Appeals rejects it, Amazon could face a different approval path under the town’s bylaws.

The local schedule is still moving. Westborough lists a Select Board meeting for Oct. 15, says the Zoning Board of Appeals is expected to hear the zoning appeal on Nov. 2, and says the Planning Board continued the site-plan hearing to Nov. 10. Those proceedings could shape the launch pad’s local approvals, but they do not replace the federal decisions required for commercial drone operations.

Amazon has said it hopes to launch Prime Air in Massachusetts by the end of the year, but the town’s page says the company requested that its Planning Board hearing be continued until after the zoning appeal. The public record therefore does not establish a launch date, a final flight pattern, the number of daily operations or how the company would address the delegation’s request. Boston.com reported that Amazon did not immediately respond to its request for comment. For Westborough and the surrounding towns, the next concrete milestones are the lawmakers’ Oct. 29 response deadline and the town’s November zoning and site-plan reviews.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Massachusetts lawmakers seek FAA review of Westborough Amazon drones
seoDescription: Four Massachusetts lawmakers want a site-specific environmental review and public comment before Amazon launches Prime Air drone deliveries from Westborough.
